title: Remove language-flavored builtin gate presets; presets resolve project-declared bundles
description:
Remove the language- and content-flavored builtin gate presets from engine code; presets stay as a mechanism resolving project-declared bundles.

## Background

`crates/jit/src/gate_presets/builtin.rs` compiles domain vocabulary into the binary: `rust-tdd`, `python-tdd`, `js-tdd`, `minimal`, and `security-audit` bundle hardcoded gate keys, titles, and checkers. This predates the current design: the preset system landed 2026-02-10 under production-polish, months before config-declared gates (@/charter/D-2) and the domain-agnostic invariant (@/inv/domain-agnostic: gate keys come from repository configuration, never from hardcoded domain assumptions). D-2's rejection rationale — every new or tuned gate requires recompiling — describes builtin bundles exactly.

The surrounding machinery is already domain-agnostic and stays: storage lists builtin and custom presets, `save_gate_preset` persists project-defined bundles, and graph templates resolve node/anchor gate names through the preset manager. The planning-bracket presets (`plan-review`, `breakdown-review`, `coverage-preview`) are workflow infrastructure of the plan bracket (@/charter/D-3), not domain vocabulary; they are what the bracket genuinely needs from this module.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The builtin preset set no longer contains language- or content-flavored bundles (`rust-tdd`, `python-tdd`, `js-tdd`, `minimal`, `security-audit`); `jit gate preset list` shows project-defined presets plus the planning-bracket presets only.
- [hard] REQ-02: The preset mechanism is unchanged for project-defined presets: save, list, show, apply, and template gate-name resolution all work against project-declared bundles; harness tests cover a project-defined preset end to end.
- [hard] REQ-03: The planning-bracket presets remain available to template role resolution, and their retention as workflow infrastructure (rather than domain content) is stated where the domain-agnostic boundary is documented.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every reference to a removed preset name is swept from CLI help text, docs/, and CLAUDE.md; `jit validate` and repo-wide search find no dangling mentions.
- [hard] REQ-05: Adopter documentation shows how to declare an equivalent bundle as a project-defined preset, replacing the removed builtins.

## Notes

Decisions pinned during intake:

- **Remove, in v1.0 scope.** A binary shipping baked-in domain vocabulary undercuts the charter's domain-agnostic claim at release. Rejected: filing without a milestone — presets are opt-in, but the contradiction is with the release's own invariant projection; and documenting a boundary exception — the invariant wording admits none for gate keys.
- **The mechanism survives, the content goes.** Project-defined presets and template resolution are config-driven and consistent with @/inv/domain-agnostic; only the compiled-in bundles violate it.
- **Planning-bracket trio retained.** `plan-review`, `breakdown-review`, `coverage-preview` encode jit's own plan-before-fan-out workflow (@/charter/D-3), not an adopter domain.
